title: CSS Grid
summary: CSS Grid arranges boxes in rows and columns at the same time.
introduction: CSS Grid arranges boxes in rows and columns at the same time. Think of squares on a board game. Make a few columns, add a gap and choose how much space each box should use.
learningObjectives: Define a grid with grid-template-columns, grid-template-rows and gap
Place items with line numbers, span and grid-template-areas
Build a responsive grid with repeat(), auto-fit and minmax()

blocks.text: Rows, columns and the fr unit

`display: grid` turns a container's direct children into grid items, and `grid-template-columns` defines the columns. Each value is a track size: a length, a percentage, `auto`, or the grid-only unit `fr`, a *fraction of the free space*. `120px 1fr 1fr` means a fixed first column and two equal columns sharing what is left. Rows are created automatically as items fill the columns, and `gap` spaces both rows and columns.

blocks.text: `repeat(3, 1fr)` is shorthand for `1fr 1fr 1fr`. `minmax(150px, 1fr)` is a track that is never narrower than 150px and otherwise shares the free space. Put the two together with the `auto-fit` keyword and the browser creates as many columns as fit, each at least 150px wide, and stretches them to fill the row. That one line is a responsive gallery with no media query at all. (`auto-fill` is the same except that it keeps empty tracks when there are few items, instead of stretching the existing ones.)

Grid lines are numbered from 1 at the start edge; a three-column grid has four vertical lines. `grid-column: 1 / 3` places an item from line 1 to line 3, two columns wide; `span 2` says the same relative to wherever the item starts, and `-1` means the last line, so `grid-column: 1 / -1` always stretches across the full width. `grid-row` works the same way, and `grid-area: row-start / column-start / row-end / column-end` sets all four at once.

blocks.text: For whole-page skeletons, `grid-template-areas` lets you *draw* the layout as strings: each string is a row, each word a cell, and repeating a name merges cells into one area. Items are assigned with `grid-area: name`. A dot (`.`) marks an empty cell. Because the drawing lives in the container's CSS, rearranging the page for a narrow screen is a matter of redrawing it inside a media query.

blocks.text: Items normally stretch to fill their cell. `justify-items` and `align-items` on the container (or `justify-self` and `align-self` on an item) change that, and `place-items: center` is the shorthand that centres content inside every cell. When the tracks together are smaller than the container, `justify-content` and `align-content` position the grid as a whole. Rows that you did not define, created when items overflow the template, are *implicit*; they are sized `auto` unless you set `grid-auto-rows`, and `grid-auto-flow: dense` lets later small items fill holes left by spanning ones.

blocks.title: 1fr can still overflow
blocks.text: `1fr` is really `minmax(auto, 1fr)`: a track can grow but cannot shrink below the minimum size of its content. A long unbroken word, a wide image or a `pre` block inside one cell therefore pushes the whole grid out of its container. Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` for the track, or `min-width: 0` on the items, when content might be wider than a column.

blocks.title: Subgrid
blocks.text: A nested grid can adopt its parent's tracks with `grid-template-columns: subgrid` (or rows). It lines up the titles, text and buttons of cards in the same row even when their content lengths differ, and all current browsers support it.

questions.question: What does `grid-column: 1 / -1` do to an item?
questions.explanation: Line 1 is the first vertical line and -1 is the last, so the item spans every column, however many there are.
options: Places it in the first column only
Moves it to the last column

questions.question: `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))` needs a media query to change the number of columns on narrow screens.
questions.explanation: The browser recomputes how many 200px-minimum columns fit every time the container's width changes, so the column count adapts without any media query.
